paragraphs: Your Tesla's battery, tracked locally over Bluetooth LE. No cloud, no account, nothing leaves the phone.

TeslaBatteryBLE talks to a Tesla over Bluetooth LE using an enrolled vehicle key — the same local protocol Tesla's vehicle-command uses. No Tesla account, no virtual-key cloud registration, no telemetry. Install the app, pair a key with an NFC card tap on the console, and read the car directly.
features: Scan & connect to nearby Teslas by advertised BLE name, with VIN-based hinting
Pair a key (CHARGINGMANAGER role by default) via Tesla's unsigned addKey flow: NFC card tap on the console + vehicle confirmation

No extra BLE channel — the car reserves one BLE channel per connected device, not per app. A dongle or keyfob always takes its own channel; the app shares your phone's link, so installed on the same phone as Tesla's…

reading is blue only while it is current (under 5 minutes old, the link up and the car awake); after that, or as soon as the link drops or the car sleeps, it turns gray and the car view, the list and the notification…
How long each state has held — the car view shows how long the car has been asleep and locked ("Asleep 1h 12m · Locked 3h · User away")

Local battery-health analytics (capacity estimation from charge sessions and rated range, charging-efficiency and parked-drain insights, habit cards), then an optional OBD path for pack-level data.
